title: Backfill compact and replant grass sods and plants in irrigation trenches

lessons.title: Backfilling and compacting the trench
lessons.html:
Backfilling and compacting the trench

After irrigation pipes are laid in a trench through an existing garden or lawn, the trench must be filled in (backfilled), packed down (compacted), and the grass and plants put back. Done well, nobody can see where the trench was after a few weeks. Done badly, the trench sinks, pipes break and plants die.

Before you backfill

  • Make sure the pipe work has been checked and pressure tested and your supervisor says you may backfill.
  • Check that no stones or sharp objects lie against the pipe.
  • Have the soil ready. During digging, the topsoil, the subsoil and the sods should have been kept in separate heaps on plastic sheets.

Steps to backfill

  1. Bed the pipe: put fine soil or sand around and just over the pipe by hand. No stones or clods. Stones can crack the pipe when the soil settles.
  2. Fill in layers: add subsoil in layers, not all at once. Each layer should be thin enough to compact properly, as your supervisor instructs.
  3. Compact each layer: tamp with a hand tamper or by foot. Do not use a heavy compactor right over the pipe until there is enough soil on top, or you may crush it.
  4. Water to settle: lightly water the backfill if instructed, to help it settle. Do not flood it.
  5. Topsoil last: put the topsoil back on top so plants and grass get good soil.
  6. Set the level: for lawn, leave the soil a sod's thickness below the surrounding lawn. Allow a little extra soil because it will settle.

Why compaction matters

Loose backfill sinks over time and leaves a dip in the lawn. Water collects in the dip, and mowers scalp the edges. Too much compaction on top makes the soil hard so roots cannot grow. Firm the subsoil well and the topsoil lightly.

lessons.title: Replanting sods and plants and cleaning up
lessons.html:
Replanting sods and plants

Grass sods

  1. Lay the sods back in the same place they came from, if possible, so the grass matches.
  2. Push the joints tight against each other and against the lawn on both sides.
  3. Fill gaps with fine topsoil.
  4. Press down with your feet or a tamper so the roots touch the soil and the surface is level with the lawn.
  5. Water well straight away. Keep it moist until the roots grow in.
  6. If sods are broken or dried out, replace them with new sods of the same grass.

Plants and shrubs

  1. Plants lifted before digging should have been kept in the shade, roots covered and moist.
  2. Dig a hole big enough for the roots.
  3. Plant at the same depth as before. Do not bury the stem deeper.
  4. Fill in with topsoil and compost, press firmly around the roots.
  5. Water well to settle the soil around the roots.
  6. Stake tall plants if needed.
  7. Mulch around plants in beds if the site uses mulch.

Cleaning up

  • Remove left-over soil, stones and rubbish.
  • Sweep paths and paving. Hose off mud if allowed.
  • Return tools clean.
  • Check that sprinklers or drippers are at the right height and not covered by soil.
  • After a week or two, check for sinking and top up with soil where needed.

Safety

  • Wear boots and gloves.
  • Lift with your legs, not your back.
  • Cover or barricade open trenches so nobody falls in.
  • Keep a safe distance from co-workers using spades and tampers.

Key points

  • Backfill only after the pipe work is tested and approved.
  • Bed the pipe in fine soil with no stones.
  • Fill and compact in layers, with topsoil last.
  • Relay sods tightly and level, and replant plants at the same depth.
  • Water at once, clean up and check later for sinking.
